name: Kugbo
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

new_statements.quote: [Kari 2017 p.3] Due to a lack of research materials or adequate research materials at the time of writing this paper, Kụgbọ, Abureni (Mini) and Ọchịchị are excluded from the discussion in the core areas of linguistics. ... [p.11, 3.4 Tone] Alex (1989:24) remarks that “all Central Delta lects operate a basic two-tone system”. These tones are low tone, which is marked with a grave accent ( ̀ ), and high tone, which is marked with an acute accent ( ´ ). There is also a downstep phenomenon in these languages. ... Apart from the syllabic nasal, tone in these languages is anchored on vowels. [Kari 2019 sec. 5.1] In all Rivers State languages, the pitch of the voice can be used to distinguish words, phrases and sentences whose segmental compositions are otherwise the same.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Kugbo is transcribed and classed as a lexical tone language (Central Delta: H and L plus downstep per Alex 1989/Kari 2017; Wolff 1969 marks five tones H/M/L/rising/falling plus length in his Abuan-group transcription, Kugbo included; Blench 2008 marks H/L on every Kugbo form). No source reached makes any statement about word stress or accent in Kugbo; the group-level phonology sections are silent on stress.
new_statements.exceptions: none; Kari 2017 explicitly says Kugbo-specific data were unavailable, so the two-tone generalisation is not verified for Kugbo (Wolff 1969's key uses five tone marks).
new_statements.domain_note: Tone described at word/lexical and grammatical level for the group; no prominence domain stated. Statements are group-level (Central Delta / all Rivers State languages), not based on Kugbo data.
new_statements.identity_note: All sources treat Kugbo (Kụgbọ, kugb1241/kes) as the language of four villages (Emago, Amoroto, Amurukeni,...) in Abua-Odual LGA (Rivers) / north Brass LGA (Bayelsa). Wolff 1969 files it as a 'dialect' (Ku) of his 'Abuan' group but Wolff 1967 and Kari 2017/2019 call it a separate language, mutually intelligible with eastern Ogbia and close to Odual. The only prosodic statements reached are group-level (Central Delta; 'all Rivers State languages'), not Kugbo-specific; the Rivers State government label 'Abureni (Kugbo)' conflates it with Abureni/Mini (abur1243), which Kari 2019 explicitly rejects.

sources.note: Nothing (zero occurrences of stress/accent as prominence). Sec. 3.4 Tone: 'all Central Delta lects operate a basic two-tone system' (H, L) plus downstep, tone anchored on vowels and syllabic nasals. Kugbo explicitly excluded from the core discussion for lack of research materials; only source listed for Kugbo is Blench (2008).

sources.note: Nothing on stress. Sec. 5.1: 'In all Rivers State languages [Kugbo is one of the 28 listed], the pitch of the voice can be used to distinguish words, phrases and sentences...'; tones attested: high, mid, low, downstepped high. Blanket areal statement, no Kugbo data.
